notes.block: Tamil, U+0B80-U+0BFF. Words are runs of its letters and signs. The Grantha letters ஜ ஶ ஷ ஸ ஹ (and க்ஷ, ஸ்ரீ as clusters) are ordinary consonants inside 0B95-0BB9.
notes.notWord: Digits ௦-௯, the old number signs ௰ ௱ ௲ and the day, month, year, debit, credit, rupee and number signs (U+0BF3-U+0BFA) are not word letters. ௐ (U+0BD0) is.
notes.firstLetter: Aytham ஃ (U+0B83) may start a word: it marks f in ஃபேஸ்புக், ஃபிரான்ஸ். Anusvara U+0B82 is not used in Tamil and can't start one.
notes.virama: The pulli (U+0BCD). Tamil shows it as a dot and has almost no conjuncts (only க்ஷ and ஸ்ரீ), so a pulli is simply 'no vowel here'.
notes.signs: Vowel signs U+0BBE-U+0BCC, the au length mark U+0BD7 and the pulli must follow a consonant. Aytham ஃ is left out: it follows a vowel (அஃது).
notes.replace: ZWJ and ZWNJ are dropped, as the engine's normal form drops them. ா + pulli is ர் typed with the wrong key, common in news text (செய்தாா் for செய்தார்): an aa sign can't carry a pulli. ஶ்ரீ (the spelling Unicode 4.1 recommends) is folded to ஸ்ரீ, which nearly all text uses. NFC already joins the two-part vowel signs (ெ + ா is ொ, ே + ா is ோ, ெ + ௗ is ௌ). ெ + ள typed for ௌ is NOT mended: தெளிவு has that sequence for real.
notes.phraseBreaks: Tamil ends sentences with Latin punctuation; the dandas are listed only for quoted Sanskrit verse.
